Sampler diagnostics for every candidate model

Source: R/check_sampling.R
check_sampling.Rd

Reports, per candidate model, whether the sampler explored the posterior: the largest Rhat, the smallest effective sample size, and the number of divergent transitions. It sits alongside check_chains (chain mixing, visually), check_priors (the priors) and check_fit (the fit against the data).

check_sampling(x, rhat_cutoff = 1.01, ess_cutoff = 400, divergence_cutoff = 10)

Arguments

x

An object of class bayesnecfit, bayesmanecfit or bayesnechurdlefit.

rhat_cutoff

A numeric vector of length 1.

ess_cutoff

A numeric vector of length 1.

divergence_cutoff

A numeric vector of length 1.

Value

A data.frame with one row per candidate model and columns model, max_rhat, min_ess, min_ess_ratio, n_divergent and failed. For a bayesnechurdlefit, a named list of two such tables — growth and survival — as rhat also returns for that class.

Details

check_sampling() asks did this model sample properly, where check_fit asks does this model reproduce the data. Both feed the same downstream question — which candidates belong in the averaged set — which is why screen_models screens on this one and reports the other beside it rather than acting on it.

Thresholds

All three are arguments; the defaults are recommendations, not rules, and whichever ships will be quoted in methods sections.

Rhat 1.01 follows Vehtari et al. (2021), which is also the reference vignette("example2") cites. rhat and summary default to the same value.

ESS 400 is Vehtari's recommendation that both bulk and tail ESS exceed 100 per chain, at the four chains bnec fits by default. The reported min_ess is the minimum over parameters of min(bulk-ESS, tail-ESS), obtained as min(neff_ratio(x)) * ndraws(x).

Divergences 10 has no literature behind it. Stan's own guidance is that any divergence means the sampler failed to explore the posterior and estimates may be biased. Ten is pragmatic, from practice with these non-linear models, which routinely produce a handful near a boundary. It is a working default and should be described that way rather than cited.

A heavily thinned fit can fail ESS that a ratio would pass

At three chains, thin = 3 and roughly a thousand retained draws, an min_ess of 400 needs a ratio of 0.40, which is demanding for these correlated non-linear parameterisations. Under bnec defaults — 8000 draws — the same cutoff is a ratio of 0.05 and is trivially met. So this screen fails some heavily thinned fits that a ratio-based screen passed. The correct response is to retain more draws, not to lower the cutoff: thinning lowers ESS by construction, and the tempting fix is the wrong one. min_ess_ratio is reported alongside so that "passed because we drew 8000" can be told apart from "passed efficiently".

Which parameters are reduced over

The same set rhat reports: the prior_* draws that sample_prior = "yes" adds are excluded, because their Rhat and ESS describe a distribution the sampler never had to explore, and a parameter with no variance is excluded because both quantities are undefined for it — which is what a constant() prior produces. failed is a logical by construction and is never NA: a model that cannot be assessed is not the same thing as a model that failed, and folding the two together silently turns screen_models into a no-op.

References

Vehtari, A., Gelman, A., Simpson, D., Carpenter, B., & Bürkner, P.-C. (2021). Rank-normalization, folding, and localization: An improved Rhat for assessing convergence of MCMC (with discussion). Bayesian Analysis, 16(2), 667–718. doi:10.1214/20-BA1221

See also

screen_models, check_fit, check_chains, rhat

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(bayesnec)
check_sampling(manec_example)
} # }
